name: Mill and Mine

stations.why: The mill's opener: a roll change locked out on the drive and the screwdown both, zero speed proven, and the crane's own path called clear before the old rolls ever come out.
PPE on before the ladle is ever approached, the splash barrier closed before the tilt starts, and every addition going in dry and through the chute, never by hand.
A battery topside worked to the plan's own heat-stress rotation, with the buddy system kept and every cooldown taken in full rather than cut short to get back to work.
A dryer-section felt change with the drive and the steam both locked out and bled to zero before the nip guard ever comes off — and the running section next door left exactly alone.
The mine's opener: a cut-and-bolt cycle that never puts a crew under roof the plan has not yet supported, with the cutting head and the crush zone respected the whole time the machine can move.
The self-rescuer donned complete before a step is taken, the alternate escapeway taken the moment the primary is found blocked, and the lifeline's own cones read by feel rather than guessed at.
The berm read against the truck's own axle before backing toward it, the spotter's signal taken before the edge, and the highwall above the dump point given the respect an unstable rock face is owed.
A belt entry's own exam: a stuck roller freed under lockout before it grinds a fire into the dust beside it, and the CO and methane monitors read and trusted rather than covered or guessed at.

summary: Four mill stations and four mine stations under one steelworkers-and-miners pack: a hot-strip stand's roll change, a ladle tilted to pour, a coke battery's heat rotation, a paper machine's felt change; then a continuous miner's cut-and-bolt cycle, an escapeway and self-rescuer drill, a haul truck's berm and dump point, and a belt entry's fire and gas exam.
union: USW steelworkers and paper crews, UMWA underground and surface mine crews
